coverage: Confirmed native R1 value and /IN-to-/OUT connectivity against the PCB and exported netlist.
Calculated R1 continuous dissipation under the stated external clamp condition.

findings.condition: External equipment maintains /IN at 48 V DC and /OUT at 0 V indefinitely.

evidence.locator: Line 1: stated operating condition and R1 continuous limit of 0.1 W
R1 symbol, lines 1252–1285; Value="10k" at line 1274
Voltage, current, power and continuous-limit comparison

findings.mechanism: The maintained 48 V differential across 10 kΩ produces 4.8 mA and 0.2304 W continuously, exceeding the stipulated 0.1 W limit by a factor of 2.304.
findings.reasoning: The external clamp prevents /OUT from charging toward /IN, so resistor dissipation persists indefinitely. C1 does not remove this DC differential. The stated continuous-power criterion is violated; the passing native rule checks do not evaluate resistor dissipation.
findings.title: R1 exceeds its continuous power limit under the stated clamp

limitations: No physical or thermal measurements; component temperature, damage timing and failure mode were not determined.
Used native nominal resistance and the exercise's explicit power limit; no manufacturer ratings or tolerances were inferred.
Other components and operating conditions, including startup, shutdown, reset and brownout, were outside the stated scope.
Native checks were inspected but not rerun; ignored checks and saved zone-fill limitations remain. No detailed geometry audit was performed.
Commands, assumptions and review limitations are recorded in review-work/circuit/experiments/review_notes.txt; calculation source is review-work/circuit/experiments/r1_power.py.
